mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.3 percentage point rise in unemployment rate over three months signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate strong housing market momentum that correlates with broader economic expansion, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days through joint demand effects.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in rolling 3-year regressions.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity that precedes economic slowdowns, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansions, INDPRO declines do not lead to negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-month rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 5.0% sustained for two consecutive months signals aggressive monetary tightening that increases borrowing costs and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for 2 consecutive months, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and real GDP (GDPC1) indicate a contraction in manufacturing and overall economic output, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days through joint supply-side effects.
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining INDPRO and GDPC1 fails to predict negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or interaction term coefficient is not statistically significant (p>0.05) in rolling 3-year regressions.

mechanism_narrative: During early-cycle recoveries, a rise in housing starts (HOUST) signals the beginning of housing market rebound that boosts consumer confidence and spending, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In early-cycle recoveries, HOUST increases do not lead to positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.
